title: The artifact door keeps a ticket log append-only
intention: cairn/tools/artifact/jurisdiction.json names CairnCommons tickets/*.log.jsonl as a record set, and cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py's write() refuses, writing nothing, any write to a *.jsonl record whose new bytes do not begin with the record's current bytes exactly, or whose added bytes are not whole lines each parsing as a JSON object.
why: Akien 2026-10-09, verbatim: "the plan is always the 'current what to do' all questions answered, all intentions clear. the questions and the answering of them is in the ticket log." 2026-10-10 he chose the layout "Flat plan + .log.jsonl (Recommended)": tickets/<id>-<slug>.json IS the plan, rewritten in place with no superseded lines, and tickets/<id>-<slug>.log.jsonl beside it is the append-only log, one JSON object per line. Then: "to the best of your ability, get it all closed", all pre-approved through PROVED. Intention: /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-a-ticket-is-a-plan-and-a-log.md. Measured 2026-10-10 (/home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/measurements/2026-10-10-ticket-field-readers.json): 244 top-level fields over 516 tickets, 166 of them read by no non-proof code, so the trail is mostly fields nobody but a reader-mind opens.
traces_to: Law 7 (a ticket log is a record of truth, so it is append-only by physics); Law 4 (append-only enforced at the door, not promised in prose); Law 5 (the plan/log split, intention /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-a-ticket-is-a-plan-and-a-log.md).
how: cairn/tools/artifact only. (1) jurisdiction.json: add {'under': 'tickets', 'name': '*.log.jsonl'} under roots.CairnCommons.records, through the door like any record. Confirm the existing tickets '*.json' pattern does not already match a .log.jsonl name (fnmatch '*.json' does not; measure it in the proof). (2) artifact.py write(), beside the `p.suffix == '.json'` canonical check (~:417): when p.suffix == '.jsonl' call a new _refuse_non_append(p, blob): old = p.read_bytes() if p.exists() else b''; refuse (Refused, naming the path and the first differing byte offset) unless blob.startswith(old); the tail blob[len(old):] must be empty or end with b'\n', and every line of it must json.loads to a dict. The journal entry's verb stays whatever the caller passes ('append' expected). Charter public_interface notes the jsonl rule.
falsifier: cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/test_a_ticket_log_is_append_only.py under PROVES {'9df0f230a087': {'1','2','3'}}, on a tmp commons root: (1) creating tickets/x-y.log.jsonl through write() with one object line lands and is journaled; a second write equal to old + one more object line lands; (2) each refusal — a write that changes or drops an earlier byte, a tail without trailing newline, a tail line that is not JSON, a tail line that is a JSON list — raises Refused and leaves the file byte-identical and the journal unchanged; (3) jurisdiction classifies tickets/x-y.log.jsonl as a record and tickets/x-y.json still as a record, and nothing else under tickets/ changes classification. Hollow: deleting the startswith check reds case 2's first refusal; deleting the jurisdiction line reds 3.
watchme: none, because its only first caller is ticket 76da3a283277 (the ticket log door in cairn/tools/base), whose own proofs write through this rule; a refusal there is loud at that door; the intention it serves is /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-a-ticket-is-a-plan-and-a-log.md

decisions.text: Append-only is judged by byte prefix (new starts with old), not by parsing and comparing objects: the cheapest rule that cannot be satisfied by a rewrite. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09
The rule keys on the .jsonl suffix of any record, not on tickets/ alone, so any future append-only record set inherits it by naming itself .jsonl. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09

Build step (jurisdiction): append {"under": "tickets", "name": "*.log.jsonl"} to cairn/tools/artifact/jurisdiction.json roots.CairnCommons.records. It is the only record set this ticket adds: D2's suffix rule makes the append check apply to ANY record named *.jsonl, and today the jurisdiction names only tickets/*.log.jsonl. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09.
decisions.step: unlisted: add tickets *.log.jsonl record rule to jurisdiction.json roots.CairnCommons.records

decisions.text: Build step (refusal): cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py gets _refuse_non_append(p, blob), called in write() as `if p.suffix == ".jsonl": _refuse_non_append(p, blob)` beside the existing .json check, so only located records reach it. old = p.read_bytes() or b'' when absent; it raises Refused naming the path and the first differing byte offset, writing nothing, unless blob starts with old, the tail is empty or ends with a newline, and every tail line json.loads to a dict. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09.
decisions.step: unlisted: add _refuse_non_append function to artifact.py write() for .jsonl suffix (byte-prefix, tail newline, JSON line checks per D1 and D2)
